totals.silver_note: First silver build complete — 66.6M campaign contributions welded

aim: Connect the untouched 172 collections (190 GB) — public records already in the vault that have never been processed. This is the standing baseline work, running every day.
Close the 618.85 GB processing gap — finish turning raw records into cleaned, keyed, connected data.
The next wave is queued: GDELT (world events), FERC energy reports, Wikidata (the world's entity graph), OpenStreetMap, and PubMed — a terabyte of new reach, staged to land.
Finish the first silver build's road: 66.6 million campaign contributions are welded and verified; the remaining 224.6 million rows are the template's next run.

Replicate the Louisiana pattern — courts welded to the people who run them — state by state. Mississippi is done at bronze; Texas is census-complete with its citation graph built; the Southeast is census-mapped (11,769,953 dockets across eight states).

The national court map is drawn: 72,998,758 dockets counted across every court in the corpus, with the federal layer fully mapped (4,600,358 dockets). Florida is the next full build — 5,464,125 dockets, sized and queued.
Named holes we say out loud: one age-adjusted health survey enumerated and never landed · nonprofit filing titles held by name · opioid shipment data (ARCOS) awaiting a decision.
raw_base_note: Covered by the national collections — campaign finance, jobs-by-county, nonprofit filings, EPA facility records, Census — in raw form. Raw is reach, not depth: it becomes knowledge when it is cleaned, keyed, and connected. That connecting work is under way state by state.
county_coverage_note: Every county in this state is reached by the national collections (jobs, facilities, nonprofits, health). County-level scans — facility by facility, city by city — are published as the connecting work reaches each state.

DC.note: The federal money lives here in substance: campaign finance, corporate filings, and federal spending — plus our data-center tracker (47 campuses, 18 incentive deals, roughly $44 billion tracked). The money is banked; the connections between it are the work ahead.

LA.note: The one finished state. Louisiana's courts are GOLD: 1,574,448 dockets and 378,406 cases, every case welded to its court and its judge — 5,565 judge profiles, and every previously anonymous author identified. Plus the officials' money: ethics filings and financial disclosures, banked. This is the pattern being replicated state by state.

MS.note: Bronze — new tonight. Mississippi's courts followed the Louisiana pattern: census settled (788,156 dockets · 84,111 cases · 89,555 opinions), the records landed, and the citation graph is built — 344,284 citing pairs inside Mississippi, plus the Fifth Circuit corridor measured both ways into Louisiana.

PA.note: Bronze. Allegheny County is mapped — 93 industrial facilities, 95.3 million pounds of toxic releases over the decade — and a 16-location dossier queue is held and ready. County work fires location by location.
